challenges.name: agent-skills-quiz
challenges.title: Will the agent open this skill?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the write-migration skill on CodeDev: a description the agent passed over, and a large reference file in the skill folder.

questions.question:
.claude/skills/add-course-seed/SKILL.md (before)
---
name: add-course-seed
description: Seed helper.
---
(35 lines: where course rows go in db/seeds, how to pick the next order index, run npm run seed:check)

Agent session, task "Add the new Rust Foundations course to the catalog":
> Skills available: add-course-seed - Seed helper.
> Editing db/seeds/catalog.sql ...
(SKILL.md is never opened; the new row reuses order index 12, which another course already has)

The team changes only the description:
description: Adds a course to the CodeDev catalog seed (row, next free order index, seed check). Use when a task adds, renames or removes a course in the catalog.

Statement: "The new description makes it more likely that the agent opens this skill for the Rust course task, because the name and description are what the agent sees when it decides whether a skill fits the task."
questions.explanation: True. Agent Skills are loaded in steps: at the start the agent only sees each skill's name and description, and it reads the body of SKILL.md when it judges that the skill fits the task. "Seed helper." says neither what the skill does nor when to use it, so nothing connects it to "add a course to the catalog". The new description names the task and the trigger (Use when ...), which is the signal the agent decides on. It is "more likely", not guaranteed: the way to verify is to rerun the same task and check in the session that SKILL.md was read and npm run seed:check was run. The misconception is that an agent reads every skill in full, so the description does not matter.

questions.question:
.claude/skills/write-migration/
  SKILL.md                    48 lines
  reference/naming.md        610 lines
  scripts/check-migration.sh

SKILL.md (excerpt)
  For new column and index names, read reference/naming.md.
  Before you finish, run scripts/check-migration.sh <file> and paste its output.

Session summary, task "Fix the typo in the leaderboard page title":
  skill metadata loaded   4 skills, about 300 tokens
  files read              app/leaderboard/page.tsx
  commands run            npm run lint

Statement: "Every session in this repository spends context on the 610 lines of reference/naming.md, so the file should be cut down or merged into SKILL.md."
questions.explanation: False. The session summary shows what was actually loaded: the short metadata of four skills and one page file. reference/naming.md is read only when the agent follows the line in SKILL.md that points to it, which happens for a migration task, not for a typo fix. That is the point of putting long reference material in its own file. Merging it into SKILL.md would make things worse: the 610 lines would then be loaded every time the skill is used, even when no new name is needed. The misconception is that everything in a skill folder is loaded into every session; check the session's files read instead of guessing.

challenges.name: validate-skill-md
challenges.title: Validate a SKILL.md in CI
challenges.description:
CodeDev keeps its Agent Skills in the repository, one folder per skill with a SKILL.md inside. After an agent ignored the write-migration skill (its name was "Write Migration" and its description "Database things."), the team wants a CI check that rejects a broken SKILL.md before any agent sees it. Write validateSkill(file). The input is one JSON object { "folder": string, "content": string }: the name of the skill's folder and the full text of its SKILL.md.

Parsing (a tiny YAML subset, no libraries):
- Treat "\r\n" as "\n". The first line must be exactly "---" (trailing spaces allowed), and a later line must be exactly "---" too. The lines between them are the frontmatter; everything after the closing line is the body. If either "---" line is missing, return ["missing frontmatter"] and nothing else.
- In the frontmatter, skip blank lines, lines whose first non-space character is "#", lines that start with a space or a tab (nested values) and lines without ":". Every other line is key: value, split at the first ":"; trim key and value. If the value is at least 2 characters long and starts and ends with the same quote (" or '), remove those two quotes. Keys appear at most once; keys other than name and description are allowed and ignored.

Checks, reported in this order (a missing or empty value counts as missing):
1. "name: missing". Otherwise, each that applies: "name: invalid characters" (it must be lowercase letters a-z and digits, in groups joined by single hyphens: no leading, trailing or double hyphen), "name: too long" (more than 64 characters), "name: does not match folder \"<folder>\"".
2. "description: missing". Otherwise, each that applies: "description: too long" (more than 1024 characters), "description: does not say when to use the skill" (it must contain "use when", in any letter case).
3. "body: empty" when the body is empty or only whitespace.

Output: the test runner prints the returned array as JSON; [] means the skill is valid.
hints: Which three parts does a SKILL.md have, and what is the earliest point at which you know a check can no longer make sense?

Split the text into lines once, find the index of the first and the closing "---" line, then handle the frontmatter lines and the body separately. Check the quote stripping and the letter case of "use when".

A similar check on another file: for "---
title: 'Release 1.3'
---
" the frontmatter has one key, title, with the value Release 1.3 (quotes removed), and the body is "" - so a rule "body must not be empty" reports it. The line "  owner: platform" starts with spaces, so it is a nested value and is skipped.

tests.name: A valid skill passes with no errors

input.content:
---
name: write-migration
description: Writes a safe Postgres migration for the CodeDev API. Use when a task adds, changes or drops a table, column or index.
---

# Write a database migration

1. Create the file with `npm run db:new -- <name>`; never edit a migration that is already merged.
2. Add new columns as nullable, backfill in batches, then add the constraint in a later migration.
3. Run `scripts/check-migration.sh` and paste its output in the pull request.
